title: The Spanish Anarchists
subtitle: The Heroic Years 1868-1936
author: Murray Bookchin
description: A history of Spanish anarchism from Fanelli's 1868 visit through the revolution of 1936.

title: Here Where We Live Is Our Country
subtitle: The Story of the Jewish Bund
author: Molly Crabapple
description: A history of the Jewish Labor Bund from the late 19th century through the Holocaust.

title: Living My Life
subtitle: An Autobiography
author: Emma Goldman
description: Emma Goldman's two-volume autobiography, spanning her arrival in America in 1885 through her deportation, her years in Soviet Russia, and her European exile.

title: No Gods, No Masters
subtitle: An Anthology of Anarchism
author: Daniel Guérin (ed.)
description: An anthology of anarchist writings spanning Stirner, Proudhon, Bakunin, Kropotkin, Malatesta, and the Spanish CNT, with editorial introductions placing each text in its historical context.

title: The Dawn of Everything
subtitle: A New History of Humanity
author: David Graeber & David Wengrow
description: A sweeping reinterpretation of human prehistory and early civilization, drawing on archaeology and anthropology to challenge linear narratives of human development.

title: A Mountain River Has Many Bends
subtitle: An Introduction to the Rojava Revolution
author: Strangers in a Tangled Wilderness
description: A short pamphlet introducing the Rojava revolution in northern Syria — its history, stateless democratic confederalism, feminist commitments, and economy.

title: Revolution in Rojava
subtitle: Democratic Autonomy and Women's Liberation in Syrian Kurdistan
author: Michael Knapp, Anja Flach & Ercan Ayboga
description: A detailed account of the Rojava Revolution: its historical roots, ideology of democratic confederalism, women's liberation, council democracy, civil-society institutions, defense, justice, economy, and ecological challenges.

title: A People's History of the United States
subtitle: 1492-Present
author: Howard Zinn
description: Howard Zinn's bottom-up retelling of US history from Columbus's arrival through the early 21st century, foregrounding indigenous peoples, slaves, workers, women, and dissenters.

title: Homage to Catalonia
author: George Orwell
description: George Orwell's first-hand account of his experiences fighting on the Republican side of the Spanish Civil War with the POUM militia in 1936-37, including the May 1937 Barcelona events.
